title: What a container is and what problem it solves

videos.script: Ana has a program that works on her machine. It needs one version of Go to build, and one version of Postgres to run. Her colleague's laptop has other versions, and so does the server. This lesson is about why that keeps going wrong, and what a container does about it. {{no-go}} First, a machine with no Go installed at all. One command later, the compiler runs anyway, inside a container. {{two-postgres}} Then two versions of Postgres on the same machine, and nothing installed for either of them. {{process}} Then the surprise. Ana starts a database in a container, and asks the host for its processes. The database is there, in the ordinary list, with an ordinary process number. A container is not a small computer. It is a process with walls around it. {{image}} And last, the two words the rest of the course stands on. An image is what you start from. A container is what is running. You will start two containers from one image, and watch them keep their files apart.
